From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Summarized scenarios (high-level) — see attached redwood-pricing-model-v2.xlsx for line-item math. Quick notes: 

Option A — Committed slab (recommended if they want predictability):
- Commitment: 30M tokens / month
- Unit price: $850 / 1M tokens (volume-discounted)
- Estimated monthly cost: $25,500
- Included burst policy: baseline routing to smaller model for tails + dedicated burst pool (up to 80 TPS for short windows, auto-failover)
- Tradeoffs: lower unit price; longer contract/commit; lower marginal cost for bursts due to reserved GPU capacity

Option B — Flexible (pay-as-you-go):
- Rate: $1,200 / 1M tokens
- If they use 25M tokens: estimated monthly cost $30,000
- Burst handling: on-demand capacity; higher per-token cost during peaks; recommended limit-based autoscale with fallback model for cost control

Sizing notes: sustained 35 TPS at expected token lengths (avg response ~120 tokens) maps to ~700k tokens/hour. Peaks at 60–80 TPS for short windows require burst pool sizing — recommend a 2x capacity buffer on first deployment, then right-size after telemetry.

Compliance: we can include SOC2 attestations and provide a Private deployment conversation if Caraway must host in VPC — that would change economics.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Ava to share both options with Liam/procurement with the spreadsheet.
2) If they prefer Option A, we draft an MSA + commitment sheet and include a 60-day performance review.
3) Book a 30-min pricing walk-through with product/ops and procurement (I can take the technical sizing).

Ben
